newsitem.title: INDIA: India Reliance posts higher first half profit.
newsitem.headline: India Reliance posts higher first half profit.

text.p: Reliance Industries on Friday posted a net profit of 6.51 billion rupees for first half 1996/97 (April-March), compared with 6.33 billion in the first half of 1995/96, confounding analysts who expected a fall.
The company also reported that first-half sales were 40.41 billion rupees, compared with 39.66 billion in the corresponding period last year.
The company, India's biggest private sector firm, made no provision for taxes at the six-month stage and said it would only make provisions at the year-end.
A Reuter survey of 14 Bombay-based analysts published on September 24 produced a consensus forecast that Reliance would show a fall to 4.67 billion rupee net profit for the first half.
The refiner and petrochemicals giant reported a gross profit of 8.22 billion rupees for the six months, up from 7.85 billion a year ago.

"The company has performed well in spite of the challenging business environment," Anil Ambani, managing director said in a statement. "This has been possible due to satisfactory volume growth and global competitiveness of all its major businesses."
